---
title: "The Three Credentials"
subtitle: "Which password opens what, and how to recover each one"
---

AppBay has three passwords. They are deliberately independent, they are never synchronized
with each other, and each is recovered by a different command.

Mixing them up is the most common way to lock yourself out of something while holding a
password that works perfectly well for something else.

## The three domains

| | What it opens | Where it lives | Recover with |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Control-plane account** | The AppBay web UI itself | `etc/control-plane/users.yaml` (mode 0600) | `appbay admin reset-password` |
| **Vault password** | `vault.enc`, your encrypted secrets | its own password file | `appbay secrets vault rotate-password` |
| **Edge user** | The apps you deployed | the edge's identity store | `appbay edge users reset-password` |

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A[operator] -->|signs in to AppBay| CP[Control-plane account]
  A -->|unlocks secrets| V[Vault password]
  U[your users] -->|sign in to deployed apps| E[Edge user]

  CP --> CPF[etc/control-plane/users.yaml]
  V --> VF[vault.enc]
  E --> EF[edge identity store]
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Why they are separate
Someone who can open Grafana must not thereby be able to reconfigure your installation, and
neither of them should be able to decrypt your secrets. Merging any two of these would make
one password enough for jobs that need different levels of trust.

This is also why AppBay never offers to "sync" them. If it did, revoking a user's access to
one app could silently change what they can do to the control plane.
:::

## Which one do I want?

**"I can't log in to the AppBay UI."**

That is the control-plane account.

```bash
appbay admin reset-password admin --generate --reveal
```

It rewrites `users.yaml`, refreshes the cache, and invalidates that user's sessions. It
does not read or touch the vault or the edge store.

**"An app asks me to sign in and my password doesn't work."**

That is an edge user — a person who signs in to a *deployed app*, not to AppBay.

```bash
appbay edge users list
appbay edge users reset-password alice --generate --reveal
```

**"A deploy failed saying a secret could not be resolved."**

That is the vault password.

```bash
appbay secrets vault rotate-password
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## A lost vault password is unrecoverable
`vault.enc` is encrypted with it. Rotation *re-encrypts* using the current password, so it
requires the current one. There is no reset — losing it means losing the stored values,
though the references to them in your manifests remain intact.
:::

## Reading a password prompt correctly

Every command that takes a password accepts three forms, and the difference matters:

```bash
# From a pipe — the value never appears in argv
printf %s "$SECRET" | appbay edge users reset-password alice --password-stdin

# Generated and shown exactly once
appbay edge users reset-password alice --generate --reveal

# Generated and NOT shown (for automation that will set it elsewhere)
appbay edge users reset-password alice --generate
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Why `--password-stdin` exists
Passing a secret as a command argument puts it in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, where every local
user can read it for the life of the process. Fine for a throwaway value in your own shell;
not fine for a configuration-management run seeding real credentials on a shared host.
:::

## What survives what

| Event | Control-plane account | Vault | Edge users |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delete `appbay.db` (the cache) | survives — rebuilt from `users.yaml` | unaffected | unaffected |
| Rotate the vault password | unaffected | re-encrypted | unaffected |
| Switch edge provider | unaffected | unaffected | store is edge-specific — see migration |
| Reinstall AppBay, same `$APPBAY_HOME` | survives | survives | survives |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Deleting the cache is safe
`appbay.db` holds sessions, job history and a query mirror — all disposable. The
authoritative record of who administers this installation is `users.yaml`, so deleting the
database logs everyone out and changes nothing else. It never reopens first-run
registration.
:::

## Retired commands

`appbay authelia` and `appbay auth` are gone. Running either prints what replaced it and
exits non-zero, so a script that still calls them fails rather than appearing to succeed.
